nodes.name: app.py
nodes.summary: Main Flask application: registers all routes for auth, book CRUD, borrow workflow, admin dashboard, likes, and Cloudinary file uploads; handles Vercel/Postgres compatibility at startup.

nodes.name: models.py
nodes.summary: SQLAlchemy ORM models for User, Book, BorrowRequest, and BookLike with relationships, soft-delete flag, and password hashing via Werkzeug.

nodes.name: config.py
nodes.summary: Flask Config class loaded from env vars; resolves DATABASE_URL with postgres:// fix for SQLAlchemy 1.4+, sets Cloudinary credentials, session lifetime, and max upload size.

nodes.name: seed_db.py
nodes.summary: Database seeder that creates sample users, books (physical and digital), and borrow requests for development and demo environments.

nodes.name: init_db.py
nodes.summary: One-time database initialisation script that creates all tables using db.create_all() within the Flask app context.

nodes.name: debug_login.py
nodes.summary: Debug script for testing login authentication logic outside of a running Flask server.

nodes.name: remote_seeder.py
nodes.summary: Hits the /admin/seed-data endpoint on a remote deployment to seed production or staging data.

nodes.name: base.html
nodes.summary: Jinja2 base template providing the shared HTML skeleton, navigation bar, flash message display, and Bootstrap imports.

nodes.name: index.html
nodes.summary: Public book catalogue page with keyword search bar and a grid of book cards showing title, author, category, and type.

nodes.name: login.html
nodes.summary: Login form template with username, password, and remember-me fields.

nodes.name: register.html
nodes.summary: User registration form template with username, email, and password fields.

nodes.name: dashboard.html
nodes.summary: Member dashboard showing the user's owned books, borrow requests they made, and borrow requests they received.

nodes.name: admin.html
nodes.summary: Admin dashboard with metrics (total users, books, active borrows, overdue), user management table, book management table, and Chart.js visualisations.

nodes.name: add_book.html
nodes.summary: Book creation form with fields for title, author, category, type (physical/digital), file upload or link, location, and description.

nodes.name: book_detail.html
nodes.summary: Book detail page showing full book info, like button, borrow button, and download link for digital books.

nodes.name: request_borrow.html
nodes.summary: Borrow request form for physical books where the borrower proposes a meeting date, time, and location.

nodes.name: style.css
nodes.summary: Application-wide CSS styles for the book management system UI.

nodes.name: conftest.py
nodes.summary: Pytest fixtures providing an in-memory SQLite test app, database, and pre-seeded admin/member users.

nodes.name: test_endpoints.py
nodes.summary: Core endpoint tests covering registration, login, book creation, borrowing, and admin actions.

nodes.name: test_features.py
nodes.summary: Feature-level tests for book likes, soft deletes, block/unblock users, and search functionality.

nodes.name: test_extended.py
nodes.summary: Extended edge-case tests covering validation errors, permission checks, and overdue borrow scenarios.

nodes.name: docker-compose.yml
nodes.summary: Docker Compose setup defining the Flask app service with environment variable injection and port binding.

nodes.name: vercel.json
nodes.summary: Vercel serverless deployment config routing all requests to the Flask WSGI app via a Python runtime.

nodes.name: User
nodes.summary: SQLAlchemy model for registered users with username, email, hashed password, role (member/admin), and is_blocked flag; uses Flask-Login UserMixin.

nodes.name: Book
nodes.summary: SQLAlchemy model for books: title, author, category, type (physical/digital), file_link, likes count, availability status, soft-delete flag, and owner relationship.

nodes.name: BorrowRequest
nodes.summary: SQLAlchemy model representing a borrow request with proposed date/time/location and status (Pending/Accepted/Rejected) linking borrower and book.

nodes.name: BookLike
nodes.summary: Association table enforcing a unique (user, book) like constraint to prevent duplicate likes.

nodes.name: ensure_ready
nodes.summary: Startup function that creates tables, runs Postgres schema migration for password_hash column, seeds admin user, and auto-seeds books if the library is empty.

nodes.name: login
nodes.summary: Login route: validates credentials, checks is_blocked, and calls Flask-Login login_user with remember-me support.

nodes.name: add_book
nodes.summary: Book creation route: validates form input, uploads file to Cloudinary (or local for dev), and persists the Book record.

nodes.name: request_borrow
nodes.summary: Creates a BorrowRequest for physical books, or immediately marks digital books as borrowed with auto-accepted status.

nodes.name: like_book
nodes.summary: Toggle like/unlike for a book: adds or removes a BookLike record and updates the denormalized likes counter on Book.

nodes.name: admin_dashboard
nodes.summary: Admin-only dashboard route that aggregates metrics: total users, books, borrow counts, overdue items, and chart data for physical vs digital split.

steps.reason: Start with configuration: database URL, Cloudinary credentials, and session settings.
Understand the four data models before reading routes.
User model with role-based access (member/admin) and block flag.
Book model supporting both physical and digital types with soft-delete.
Borrow workflow state machine: Pending → Accepted/Rejected.
All routes live here: auth, books, borrowing, admin, likes.
Called at startup to bootstrap the database, admin user, and seed data.

tours.title: Core Data Flow — Borrowing a Book

steps.reason: User browses the public catalogue and searches for a book.
User views book detail, sees like button and borrow request form.
POST handler creates a BorrowRequest (physical) or auto-accepts it (digital).
Request record holds proposed meeting details and transitions through status states.
Both owner and borrower see request status in their personal dashboards.
Admin sees all requests, overdue items, and aggregate metrics.
